asserts: The wire enums are closed sets with these exact codes: ten dtypes 0..9, two aggregation modes, two timing modes, two timing-flag bits, two file states, two scaling types, and the compression/profile codes; an unrecognised value in any of them is a read-time rejection, never a default.
source: the enum definitions in spec/v1, cross-checked against the dtype widths and the recipe registry the rest of the corpus uses
contract: An enum is a closed set: a reader that defaults an unknown value reads a file its writer never wrote.

cases.name: enum/dtype
cases.note: the wire dtype enum: an implementation's dtype type carries these exact codes

cases.name: enum/aggregation_mode
cases.note: bitfield mode is rejected at read time on a float dtype

cases.name: enum/timing_mode
cases.note: timing is a property of the GROUP, not the block

cases.name: enum/file_state
cases.note: one byte at header offset 13; there is NO per-block open/closed flag

cases.name: enum/scaling_type
cases.note: a linear channel stores float64 gain then float64 offset in scaling_params

cases.name: enum/timing_flags
cases.note: a set reserved bit is rejected at open

cases.name: enum/compression_id-v1-profile
cases.note: v1 reinterprets the field as the file PROFILE: 0 = none, where every recipe byte must be 0x00 (the interchange and conformance profile); 2 = recipe. Every other value, 1 included, is reserved and rejected

cases.name: enum/recipe-registry-v1
cases.note: one recipe byte per stream. Every other value is reserved and rejected with an actionable error naming the byte; there is no registry escape

cases.name: dtype-widths
cases.note: byte width per dtype; a bucket tuple is 4 * width, a position pair is 16
